decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this sentence to acknowledge that improving vaccination rates are helping slow the spread of the virus.

changes.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed this dark assessment of the pandemic, signaling an improving tone regarding the health crisis.

changes.quote: Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain.
changes.explanation: This updated wording highlights optimism that vaccinations will keep easing pandemic economic drag, even though risks still exist.

tone_quotes.quote: Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States.

The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.75% APR costs about $61.46 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.57% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.99% would rise by about $9.72 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.8%, and employers added an average of 562k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.9% over the past year (May 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 6.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +5 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.54%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.21% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will maintain its current policy stance until substantial further progress is made toward maximum employment and price stability.
